scenes.setting: Athens. A hall in Timon’s house

lines.text: Enter Poet, Painter, Jeweller and Merchant at several doors.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Good day, sir.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: I am glad you’re well.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: I have not seen you long. How goes the world?

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: It wears, sir, as it grows.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Ay, that’s well known.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: But what particular rarity? What strange,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Which manifold record not matches? See,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Magic of bounty, all these spirits thy power

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Hath conjured to attend! I know the merchant.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: I know them both. Th’ other’s a jeweller.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: O, ’tis a worthy lord!

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: Nay, that’s most fixed.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: A most incomparable man, breathed, as it were,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: To an untirable and continuate goodness.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: He passes.

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: I have a jewel here—

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: O, pray let’s see’t. For the Lord Timon, sir?

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: If he will touch the estimate. But for that—

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: When we for recompense have praised the vile,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: It stains the glory in that happy verse

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Which aptly sings the good.
[_Looking at the jewel_.]

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: ’Tis a good form.

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: And rich. Here is a water, look ye.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: You are rapt, sir, in some work, some dedication

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: To the great lord.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: A thing slipped idly from me.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Our poesy is as a gum which oozes

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: From whence ’tis nourished. The fire i’ th’ flint

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Shows not till it be struck; our gentle flame

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Provokes itself and, like the current, flies

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Each bound it chases. What have you there?

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: A picture, sir. When comes your book forth?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Upon the heels of my presentment, sir.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Let’s see your piece.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: ’Tis a good piece.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: So ’tis. This comes off well and excellent.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: Indifferent.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Admirable! How this grace

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Speaks his own standing! What a mental power

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: This eye shoots forth! How big imagination

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Moves in this lip! To th’ dumbness of the gesture

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: One might interpret.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: It is a pretty mocking of the life.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: Here is a touch. Is’t good?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: I’ll say of it,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: It tutors nature. Artificial strife

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Lives in these touches livelier than life.
Enter certain Senators, who pass over the stage.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: How this lord is followed!

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: The senators of Athens, happy men!

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: Look, more!

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: You see this confluence, this great flood of visitors.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: I have in this rough work shaped out a man

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Whom this beneath world doth embrace and hug

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: With amplest entertainment. My free drift

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Halts not particularly, but moves itself

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: In a wide sea of wax. No levelled malice

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Infects one comma in the course I hold,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: But flies an eagle flight, bold and forth on,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Leaving no tract behind.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: How shall I understand you?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: I will unbolt to you.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: You see how all conditions, how all minds,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: As well of glib and slipp’ry creatures as

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Of grave and austere quality, tender down

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Their services to Lord Timon. His large fortune,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Upon his good and gracious nature hanging,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Subdues and properties to his love and tendance

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: All sorts of hearts; yea, from the glass-faced flatterer

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: To Apemantus, that few things loves better

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Than to abhor himself; even he drops down

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: The knee before him and returns in peace

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Most rich in Timon’s nod.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: I saw them speak together.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Sir, I have upon a high and pleasant hill

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Feigned Fortune to be throned. The base o’ th’ mount

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Is ranked with all deserts, all kind of natures

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: That labour on the bosom of this sphere

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: To propagate their states. Amongst them all

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Whose eyes are on this sovereign lady fixed,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: One do I personate of Lord Timon’s frame,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Whom Fortune with her ivory hand wafts to her,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Whose present grace to present slaves and servants

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Translates his rivals.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: ’Tis conceived to scope.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: This throne, this Fortune, and this hill, methinks,

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: With one man beckoned from the rest below,

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: Bowing his head against the steepy mount

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: To climb his happiness, would be well expressed

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: In our condition.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Nay, sir, but hear me on.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: All those which were his fellows but of late,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Some better than his value, on the moment

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Follow his strides, his lobbies fill with tendance,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Rain sacrificial whisperings in his ear,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Make sacred even his stirrup, and through him

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Drink the free air.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: Ay, marry, what of these?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: When Fortune in her shift and change of mood

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Spurns down her late beloved, all his dependants,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Which laboured after him to the mountain’s top

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Even on their knees and hands, let him slip down,

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Not one accompanying his declining foot.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: ’Tis common.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: A thousand moral paintings I can show

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: That shall demonstrate these quick blows of Fortune’s

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: More pregnantly than words. Yet you do well

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: To show Lord Timon that mean eyes have seen

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: The foot above the head.
Trumpets sound. Enter Lord Timon, addressing himself courteously to every suitor. He is accompanied by a Messenger; Lucilius and other servants follow.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Imprisoned is he, say you?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Ay, my good lord. Five talents is his debt,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: His means most short, his creditors most strait.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Your honourable letter he desires

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To those have shut him up, which, failing,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Periods his comfort.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Noble Ventidius. Well,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I am not of that feather to shake off

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: My friend when he must need me. I do know him

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: A gentleman that well deserves a help,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Which he shall have. I’ll pay the debt and free him.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Your lordship ever binds him.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Commend me to him, I will send his ransom;

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And, being enfranchised, bid him come to me.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: ’Tis not enough to help the feeble up,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: But to support him after. Fare you well.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: All happiness to your honour.
[_Exit._]
Enter an Old Athenian.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Lord Timon, hear me speak.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Freely, good father.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Thou hast a servant named Lucilius.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I have so. What of him?

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Most noble Timon, call the man before thee.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Attends he here or no? Lucilius!

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Here, at your lordship’s service.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: This fellow here, Lord Timon, this thy creature,

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: By night frequents my house. I am a man

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: That from my first have been inclined to thrift,

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: And my estate deserves an heir more raised

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Than one which holds a trencher.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Well, what further?

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: One only daughter have I, no kin else,

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: On whom I may confer what I have got.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: The maid is fair, o’ th’ youngest for a bride,

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: And I have bred her at my dearest cost

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: In qualities of the best. This man of thine

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Attempts her love. I prithee, noble lord,

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Join with me to forbid him her resort;

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Myself have spoke in vain.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: The man is honest.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Therefore he will be, Timon.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: His honesty rewards him in itself;

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: It must not bear my daughter.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Does she love him?

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: She is young and apt.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Our own precedent passions do instruct us

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: What levity’s in youth.
[_To Lucilius_.]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Love you the maid?

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Ay, my good lord, and she accepts of it.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: If in her marriage my consent be missing,

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: I call the gods to witness, I will choose

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Mine heir from forth the beggars of the world

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: And dispossess her all.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How shall she be endowed,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: If she be mated with an equal husband?

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Three talents on the present; in future, all.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: This gentleman of mine hath served me long.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To build his fortune I will strain a little,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: For ’tis a bond in men. Give him thy daughter.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What you bestow, in him I’ll counterpoise,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And make him weigh with her.

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Most noble lord,

lines.speaker: OLD ATHENIAN
lines.text: Pawn me to this your honour, she is his.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: My hand to thee; mine honour on my promise.

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Humbly I thank your lordship. Never may

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: That state or fortune fall into my keeping

lines.speaker: LUCILIUS
lines.text: Which is not owed to you.
[_Exeunt Lucilius and Old Athenian._]
[_Presenting his poem_.]

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Vouchsafe my labour, and long live your lordship.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I thank you, you shall hear from me anon.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Go not away.—What have you there, my friend?

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: A piece of painting, which I do beseech

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: Your lordship to accept.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Painting is welcome.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: The painting is almost the natural man,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: For since dishonour traffics with man’s nature,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: He is but outside; these pencilled figures are

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Even such as they give out. I like your work,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And you shall find I like it. Wait attendance

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Till you hear further from me.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: The gods preserve you.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Well fare you, gentleman. Give me your hand.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: We must needs dine together. Sir, your jewel

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Hath suffered under praise.

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: What, my lord, dispraise?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: A mere satiety of commendations.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: If I should pay you for ’t as ’tis extolled,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: It would unclew me quite.

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: My lord, ’tis rated

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: As those which sell would give. But you well know

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: Things of like value, differing in the owners,

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: Are prized by their masters. Believe’t, dear lord,

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: You mend the jewel by the wearing it.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Well mocked.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: No, my good lord, he speaks the common tongue,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Which all men speak with him.
Enter Apemantus.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Look who comes here. Will you be chid?

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: We’ll bear, with your lordship.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: He’ll spare none.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Good morrow to thee, gentle Apemantus.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Till I be gentle, stay thou for thy good morrow—

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: When thou art Timon’s dog, and these knaves honest.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Why dost thou call them knaves? Thou know’st them not.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Are they not Athenians?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Then I repent not.

lines.speaker: JEWELLER
lines.text: You know me, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Thou know’st I do, I called thee by thy name.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Thou art proud, Apemantus.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Of nothing so much as that I am not like Timon.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Whither art going?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: To knock out an honest Athenian’s brains.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: That’s a deed thou’lt die for.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Right, if doing nothing be death by th’ law.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How lik’st thou this picture, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: The best, for the innocence.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Wrought he not well that painted it?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: He wrought better that made the painter, and yet he’s but a filthy

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: piece of work.

lines.speaker: PAINTER
lines.text: You’re a dog.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Thy mother’s of my generation. What’s she, if I be a dog?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Wilt dine with me, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: No, I eat not lords.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: An thou shouldst, thou’dst anger ladies.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: O, they eat lords. So they come by great bellies.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: That’s a lascivious apprehension.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: So thou apprehend’st it, take it for thy labour.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How dost thou like this jewel, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Not so well as plain-dealing, which will not cost a man a doit.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What dost thou think ’tis worth?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Not worth my thinking. How now, poet?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: How now, philosopher?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Thou liest.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Art not one?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Then I lie not.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Art not a poet?

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Then thou liest. Look in thy last work, where thou hast feigned him a

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: worthy fellow.

lines.speaker: POET
lines.text: That’s not feigned, he is so.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Yes, he is worthy of thee, and to pay thee for thy labour. He that

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: loves to be flattered is worthy o’ th’ flatterer. Heavens, that I were

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: a lord!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What wouldst do then, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: E’en as Apemantus does now, hate a lord with my heart.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What, thyself?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Ay.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Wherefore?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: That I had no angry wit to be a lord. Art not thou a merchant?

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Ay, Apemantus.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Traffic confound thee, if the gods will not.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: If traffic do it, the gods do it.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Traffic’s thy god, and thy god confound thee!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Trumpet sounds. Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What trumpet’s that?

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: ’Tis Alcibiades, and some twenty horse,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: All of companionship.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Pray entertain them, give them guide to us.
[_Exeunt some Attendants._]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You must needs dine with me. Go not you hence

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Till I have thanked you; when dinner’s done,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Show me this piece. I am joyful of your sights.
Enter Alcibiades with his company.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Most welcome, sir.
[_They bow to each other._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: So, so, there!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Aches contract and starve your supple joints!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: That there should be small love amongst these sweet knaves,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: And all this courtesy! The strain of man’s bred out

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Into baboon and monkey.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Sir, you have saved my longing, and I feed

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Most hungerly on your sight.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Right welcome, sir!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Ere we depart we’ll share a bounteous time

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: In different pleasures. Pray you, let us in.
[_Exeunt all but Apemantus._]
Enter two Lords.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: What time o’ day is’t, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Time to be honest.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: That time serves still.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: The more accursed thou, that still omitt’st it.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Thou art going to Lord Timon’s feast?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Ay, to see meat fill knaves and wine heat fools.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Fare thee well, fare thee well.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Thou art a fool to bid me farewell twice.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Why, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Shouldst have kept one to thyself, for I mean to give thee none.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Hang thyself!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: No, I will do nothing at thy bidding. Make thy requests to thy friend.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Away, unpeaceable dog, or I’ll spurn thee hence.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I will fly, like a dog, the heels o’ th’ ass.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: He’s opposite to humanity. Come, shall we in

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: And taste Lord Timon’s bounty? He outgoes

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The very heart of kindness.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: He pours it out; Plutus, the god of gold,

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Is but his steward. No meed but he repays

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Sevenfold above itself, no gift to him

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: But breeds the giver a return exceeding

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: All use of quittance.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The noblest mind he carries

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: That ever governed man.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Long may he live in fortunes. Shall we in?

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I’ll keep you company.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The Same. A room of state in Timon’s house

lines.text: Hautboys playing loud music. A great banquet served in, Flavius and others attending; and then enter Lord Timon,  the Senators, the Athenian Lords, Alcibiades, and Ventidius, which Timon redeemded from prison. Then comes, dropping after all, Apemantus, discontentedly, like himself.

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: Most honoured Timon,

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: It hath pleased the gods to remember my father’s age

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: And call him to long peace.

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: He is gone happy and has left me rich.

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: Then, as in grateful virtue I am bound

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: To your free heart, I do return those talents,

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: Doubled with thanks and service, from whose help

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: I derived liberty.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: O, by no means,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Honest Ventidius. You mistake my love.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I gave it freely ever, and there’s none

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Can truly say he gives if he receives.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: If our betters play at that game, we must not dare

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To imitate them; faults that are rich are fair.

lines.speaker: VENTIDIUS
lines.text: A noble spirit!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Nay, my lords, ceremony was but devised at first

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To set a gloss on faint deeds, hollow welcomes,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Recanting goodness, sorry ere ’tis shown;

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: But where there is true friendship there needs none.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Pray, sit, more welcome are ye to my fortunes

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Than my fortunes to me.
[_They sit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: My lord, we always have confessed it.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Ho, ho, confessed it? Hanged it, have you not?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: O Apemantus, you are welcome.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: No,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: You shall not make me welcome.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I come to have thee thrust me out of doors.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Fie, thou’rt a churl, ye’ve got a humour there

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Does not become a man; ’tis much to blame.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: They say, my lords, _ira furor brevis est_,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: But yond man is ever angry.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Go, let him have a table by himself,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: For he does neither affect company,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Nor is he fit for it indeed.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Let me stay at thine apperil, Timon.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I come to observe; I give thee warning on’t.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I take no heed of thee. Thou’rt an Athenian, therefore, welcome. I

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: myself would have no power; prithee; let my meat make thee silent.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I scorn thy meat, ’twould choke me, for I should ne’er flatter thee. O

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: you gods, what a number of men eats Timon, and he sees ’em not! It

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: grieves me to see so many dip their meat in one man’s blood; and all

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: the madness is, he cheers them up too.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I wonder men dare trust themselves with men.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Methinks they should invite them without knives.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Good for their meat, and safer for their lives.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: There’s much example for ’t. The fellow that sits next him, now parts

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: bread with him, pledges the breath of him in a divided draft, is the

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: readiest man to kill him. ’T has been proved. If I were a huge man, I

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: should fear to drink at meals,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Lest they should spy my wind-pipe’s dangerous notes.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Great men should drink with harness on their throats.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: My lord, in heart, and let the health go round.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Let it flow this way, my good lord.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Flow this way? A brave fellow! He keeps his tides well. Those healths

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: will make thee and thy state look ill, Timon.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Here’s that which is too weak to be a sinner,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Honest water, which ne’er left man i’ the mire.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: This and my food are equals, there’s no odds.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Feasts are too proud to give thanks to the gods.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: _Apemantus’ grace_

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Immortal gods, I crave no pelf,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I pray for no man but myself.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Grant I may never prove so fond

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: To trust man on his oath or bond,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Or a harlot for her weeping,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Or a dog that seems a-sleeping,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Or a keeper with my freedom,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Or my friends if I should need ’em.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Amen. So fall to’t.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Rich men sin, and I eat root.
[_He eats and drinks._]

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Much good dich thy good heart, Apemantus!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Captain Alcibiades, your heart’s in the field now.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: My heart is ever at your service, my lord.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You had rather be at a breakfast of enemies than a dinner of friends.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: So they were bleeding new, my lord, there’s no meat like ’em. I could

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: wish my best friend at such a feast.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Would all those flatterers were thine enemies then, that then thou

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: mightst kill ’em, and bid me to ’em.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Might we but have that happiness, my lord, that you would once use our

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: hearts, whereby we might express some part of our zeals, we should

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: think ourselves for ever perfect.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: O, no doubt, my good friends, but the gods themselves have provided

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: that I shall have much help from you. How had you been my friends else?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Why have you that charitable title from thousands, did not you chiefly

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: belong to my heart? I have told more of you to myself than you can with

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: modesty speak in your own behalf. And thus far I confirm you. O you

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: gods, think I, what need we have any friends if we should ne’er have

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: need of ’em? They were the most needless creatures living, should we

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: ne’er have use for ’em, and would most resemble sweet instruments hung

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: up in cases, that keep their sounds to themselves. Why, I have often

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: wished myself poorer that I might come nearer to you. We are born to do

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: benefits, and what better or properer can we call our own than the

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: riches of our friends? O, what a precious comfort ’tis to have so many,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: like brothers, commanding one another’s fortunes. O joy’s e’en made

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: away ere’t can be born! Mine eyes cannot hold out water, methinks. To

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: forget their faults, I drink to you.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Thou weep’st to make them drink, Timon.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Joy had the like conception in our eyes

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: And, at that instant like a babe sprung up.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Ho, ho! I laugh to think that babe a bastard.

lines.speaker: THIRD LORD
lines.text: I promise you, my lord, you moved me much.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Much!
[_A tucket sounds._]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What means that trump?
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How now?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Please you, my lord, there are certain ladies most desirous of

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: admittance.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Ladies? What are their wills?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: There comes with them a forerunner, my lord, which bears that office,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: to signify their pleasures.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I pray, let them be admitted.
[_Exit Servant._]
Enter Cupid.

lines.speaker: CUPID
lines.text: Hail to thee, worthy Timon, and to all

lines.speaker: CUPID
lines.text: That of his bounties taste! The five best senses

lines.speaker: CUPID
lines.text: Acknowledge thee their patron and come freely

lines.speaker: CUPID
lines.text: To gratulate thy plenteous bosom. There

lines.speaker: CUPID
lines.text: Taste, touch, all, pleased from thy table rise;

lines.speaker: CUPID
lines.text: They only now come but to feast thine eyes.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: They’re welcome all, let ’em have kind admittance.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Music, make their welcome!

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: You see, my lord, how ample you’re beloved.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Music. Enter a masque of Ladies as Amazons, with lutes in their hands,

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: dancing and playing.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Hoy-day!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: What a sweep of vanity comes this way.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: They dance? They are madwomen.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Like madness is the glory of this life,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: As this pomp shows to a little oil and root.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: We make ourselves fools to disport ourselves,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: And spend our flatteries to drink those men

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Upon whose age we void it up again

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: With poisonous spite and envy.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Who lives that’s not depraved or depraves?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Who dies that bears not one spurn to their graves

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Of their friend’s gift?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I should fear those that dance before me now

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Would one day stamp upon me. ’T has been done.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Men shut their doors against a setting sun.
[_The Lords rise from table, with much adoring of Timon, and to show their loves each singles out an Amazon, and all dance, men with women, a lofty strain or two to the hautboys, and cease._]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You have done our pleasures much grace, fair ladies,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Set a fair fashion on our entertainment,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Which was not half so beautiful and kind.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You have added worth unto ’t and lustre,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And entertained me with mine own device.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I am to thank you for ’t.

lines.speaker: FIRST LADY
lines.text: My lord, you take us even at the best.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Faith, for the worst is filthy and would not hold taking, I doubt me.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Ladies, there is an idle banquet attends you,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Please you to dispose yourselves.

lines.speaker: ALL LADIES
lines.text: Most thankfully, my lord.
[_Exeunt Cupid and Ladies._]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Flavius!

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: My lord?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: The little casket bring me hither.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Yes, my lord. [_Aside_.] More jewels yet?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: There is no crossing him in ’s humour;

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Else I should tell him well, i’ faith, I should,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: When all’s spent, he’d be crossed then, an he could.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: ’Tis pity bounty had not eyes behind,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: That man might ne’er be wretched for his mind.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: Where be our men?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Here, my lord, in readiness.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: Our horses!
Enter Flavius with the casket.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: O, my friends, I have one word

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To say to you. Look you, my good lord,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I must entreat you, honour me so much

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: As to advance this jewel. Accept it and wear it,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Kind my lord.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: I am so far already in your gifts—

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: So are we all.
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: My lord, there are certain nobles of the Senate

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Newly alighted and come to visit you.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: They are fairly welcome.
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I beseech your honour,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Vouchsafe me a word. It does concern you near.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Near? Why then, another time I’ll hear thee.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I prithee let’s be provided to show them entertainment.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I scarce know how.
Enter another Servant.

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: May it please your honour, Lord Lucius,

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: Out of his free love, hath presented to you

lines.speaker: SECOND SERVANT
lines.text: Four milk-white horses, trapped in silver.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I shall accept them fairly; let the presents

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Be worthily entertained.
[_Exit Servant._]
Enter a third Servant.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How now? What news?

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: Please you, my lord, that honourable gentleman, Lord Lucullus, entreats

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: your company tomorrow to hunt with him and has sent your honour two

lines.speaker: THIRD SERVANT
lines.text: brace of greyhounds.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I’ll hunt with him; and let them be received,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Not without fair reward.
[_Exit Servant._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: What will this come to?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: He commands us to provide, and give great gifts,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And all out of an empty coffer;

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Nor will he know his purse or yield me this:

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: To show him what a beggar his heart is,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Being of no power to make his wishes good.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: His promises fly so beyond his state

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: That what he speaks is all in debt; he owes

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: For every word. He is so kind that he now

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Pays interest for ’t; his land’s put to their books.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Well, would I were gently put out of office

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Before I were forced out.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Happier is he that has no friend to feed

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Than such that do e’en enemies exceed.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I bleed inwardly for my lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You do yourselves much wrong,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You bate too much of your own merits.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Here, my lord, a trifle of our love.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: With more than common thanks I will receive it.

lines.speaker: THIRD LORD
lines.text: O, he’s the very soul of bounty!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And now I remember, my lord, you gave good words the other day of a bay

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: courser I rode on. ’Tis yours because you liked it.

lines.speaker: THIRD LORD
lines.text: O, I beseech you, pardon me, my lord, in that.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You may take my word, my lord. I know no man

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Can justly praise but what he does affect.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I weigh my friend’s affection with mine own.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I’ll tell you true, I’ll call to you.

lines.speaker: ALL LORDS
lines.text: O, none so welcome!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I take all and your several visitations

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: So kind to heart, ’tis not enough to give;

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Methinks I could deal kingdoms to my friends,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And ne’er be weary. Alcibiades,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Thou art a soldier, therefore seldom rich.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: It comes in charity to thee, for all thy living

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Is ’mongst the dead, and all the lands thou hast

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Lie in a pitched field.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Ay, defiled land, my lord.

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: We are so virtuously bound—

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And so am I to you.

lines.speaker: SECOND LORD
lines.text: So infinitely endeared—

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: All to you. Lights, more lights!

lines.speaker: FIRST LORD
lines.text: The best of happiness, honour, and fortunes keep with you, Lord Timon.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Ready for his friends.
[_Exeunt all but Apemantus and Timon._]

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: What a coil’s here!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Serving of becks and jutting out of bums!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I doubt whether their legs be worth the sums

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: That are given for ’em. Friendship’s full of dregs.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Methinks false hearts should never have sound legs.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Thus honest fools lay out their wealth on curtsies.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Now, Apemantus, if thou wert not sullen,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I would be good to thee.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: No, I’ll nothing, for if I should be bribed too, there would be none

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: left to rail upon thee, and then thou wouldst sin the faster. Thou

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: giv’st so long, Timon, I fear me thou wilt give away thyself in paper

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: shortly. What needs these feasts, pomps, and vainglories?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Nay, an you begin to rail on society once, I am sworn not to give

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: regard to you. Farewell, and come with better music.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: So. Thou wilt not hear me now, thou shalt not then.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: I’ll lock thy heaven from thee.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: O, that men’s ears should be

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: To counsel deaf, but not to flattery!
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Athens. A room in a senator’s house

lines.text: Enter a Senator with papers.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: And late five thousand. To Varro and to Isidore

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: He owes nine thousand, besides my former sum,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Which makes it five-and-twenty. Still in motion

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Of raging waste! It cannot hold; it will not.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: If I want gold, steal but a beggar’s dog

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: And give it Timon, why, the dog coins gold.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: If I would sell my horse, and buy twenty more

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Better than he, why, give my horse to Timon—

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Ask nothing, give it him—it foals me straight,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: And able horses. No porter at his gate,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: But rather one that smiles and still invites

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: All that pass by. It cannot hold; no reason

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Can sound his state in safety. Caphis, ho!

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Caphis, I say!
Enter Caphis.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Here, sir, what is your pleasure?

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Get on your cloak and haste you to Lord Timon.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Importune him for my moneys; be not ceased

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: With slight denial, nor then silenced when

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: “Commend me to your master”, and the cap

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Plays in the right hand, thus; but tell him,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: My uses cry to me, I must serve my turn

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Out of mine own, his days and times are past,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: And my reliances on his fracted dates

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Have smit my credit. I love and honour him,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: But must not break my back to heal his finger.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Immediate are my needs, and my relief

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Must not be tossed and turned to me in words,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: But find supply immediate. Get you gone.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Put on a most importunate aspect,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: A visage of demand, for I do fear

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: When every feather sticks in his own wing,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Lord Timon will be left a naked gull,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Which flashes now a phoenix. Get you gone.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: I go, sir.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Take the bonds along with you,

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: And have the dates in. Come.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: I will, sir.

lines.speaker: SENATOR
lines.text: Go.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A hall in Timon’s house

lines.text: Enter Flavius with many bills in his hand.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: No care, no stop, so senseless of expense,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: That he will neither know how to maintain it

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Nor cease his flow of riot. Takes no account

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: How things go from him, nor resumes no care

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Of what is to continue. Never mind

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Was to be so unwise, to be so kind.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: What shall be done? He will not hear till feel.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I must be round with him, now he comes from hunting.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Fie, fie, fie, fie!
Enter Caphis and the Servants of Isidore and Varro.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Good even, Varro. What, you come for money?

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Is’t not your business too?

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: It is. And yours too, Isidore?

lines.speaker: ISIDORE’S SERVANT
lines.text: It is so.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Would we were all discharged!

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: I fear it.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Here comes the lord.
Enter Timon and his train with Alcibiades

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: So soon as dinner’s done, we’ll forth again,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: My Alcibiades. With me? What is your will?

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: My lord, here is a note of certain dues.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Dues? Whence are you?

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Of Athens here, my lord.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Go to my steward.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Please it your lordship, he hath put me off

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: To the succession of new days this month.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: My master is awaked by great occasion

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: To call upon his own and humbly prays you

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: That with your other noble parts you’ll suit

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: In giving him his right.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Mine honest friend,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I prithee but repair to me next morning.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Nay, good my lord—

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Contain thyself, good friend.

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: One Varro’s servant, my good lord—

lines.speaker: ISIDORE’S SERVANT
lines.text: From Isidore. He humbly prays your speedy payment.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: If you did know, my lord, my master’s wants—

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: ’Twas due on forfeiture, my lord, six weeks and past.

lines.speaker: ISIDORE’S SERVANT
lines.text: Your steward puts me off, my lord, and I

lines.speaker: ISIDORE’S SERVANT
lines.text: Am sent expressly to your lordship.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Give me breath.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I do beseech you, good my lords, keep on,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I’ll wait upon you instantly.
[_Exeunt Alcibiades and Timon’s train._]
[_To Flavius_.]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Come hither. Pray you,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How goes the world, that I am thus encountered

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: With clamorous demands of debt, broken bonds,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And the detention of long-since-due debts

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Against my honour?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Please you, gentlemen,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: The time is unagreeable to this business.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Your importunacy cease till after dinner,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: That I may make his lordship understand

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Wherefore you are not paid.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Do so, my friends.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: See them well entertained.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Pray, draw near.
[_Exit._]
Enter Apemantus and Fool.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Stay, stay, here comes the fool with Apemantus.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Let’s ha’ some sport with ’em.

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Hang him, he’ll abuse us.

lines.speaker: ISIDORE’S SERVANT
lines.text: A plague upon him, dog!

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: How dost, fool?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Dost dialogue with thy shadow?

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: I speak not to thee.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: No, ’tis to thyself.
[_To the Fool_.]

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Come away.
[_To Varro’s servant_.]

lines.speaker: ISIDORE’S SERVANT
lines.text: There’s the fool hangs on your back already.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: No, thou stand’st single; thou’rt not on him yet.

lines.speaker: CAPHIS
lines.text: Where’s the fool now?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: He last asked the question. Poor rogues and usurers’ men, bawds between

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: gold and want.

lines.speaker: ALL SERVANTS
lines.text: What are we, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Asses.

lines.speaker: ALL SERVANTS
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: That you ask me what you are, and do not know yourselves. Speak to ’em,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: fool.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: How do you, gentlemen?

lines.speaker: ALL SERVANTS
lines.text: Gramercies, good fool. How does your mistress?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: She’s e’en setting on water to scald such chickens as you are. Would we

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: could see you at Corinth!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Good, gramercy.
Enter Page.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Look you, here comes my mistress’ page.
[_To the Fool_.]

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Why, how now, captain? What do you in this wise

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: company? How dost thou, Apemantus?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Would I had a rod in my mouth, that I might answer thee profitably.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Prithee, Apemantus, read me the superscription of these letters. I know

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: not which is which.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Canst not read?

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: There will little learning die, then, that day thou art hanged. This is

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: to Lord Timon, this to Alcibiades. Go, thou wast born a bastard, and

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: thou’lt die a bawd.

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: Thou wast whelped a dog, and thou shalt famish a dog’s death. Answer

lines.speaker: PAGE
lines.text: not; I am gone.
[_Exit Page._]

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: E’en so thou outrunn’st grace. Fool, I will go with you to Lord

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Timon’s.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Will you leave me there?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: If Timon stay at home.—You three serve three usurers?

lines.speaker: ALL SERVANTS
lines.text: Ay, would they served us!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: So would I—as good a trick as ever hangman served thief.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Are you three usurers’ men?

lines.speaker: ALL SERVANTS
lines.text: Ay, fool.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: I think no usurer but has a fool to his servant. My mistress is one,

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: and I am her fool. When men come to borrow of your masters, they

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: approach sadly and go away merry, but they enter my mistress’s house

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: merrily and go away sadly. The reason of this?

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: I could render one.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Do it then, that we may account thee a whoremaster and a knave, which

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: notwithstanding, thou shalt be no less esteemed.

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: What is a whoremaster, fool?

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: A fool in good clothes, and something like thee. ’Tis a spirit;

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: sometime ’t appears like a lord, sometime like a lawyer, sometime like

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: a philosopher, with two stones more than’s artificial one. He is very

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: often like a knight; and generally, in all shapes that man goes up and

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: down in from fourscore to thirteen, this spirit walks in.

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Thou art not altogether a fool.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: Nor thou altogether a wise man. As much foolery as I have, so much wit

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: thou lack’st.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: That answer might have become Apemantus.

lines.speaker: VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Aside, aside, here comes Lord Timon.
Enter Timon and Flavius.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Come with me, fool, come.

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: I do not always follow lover, elder brother, and woman; sometime the

lines.speaker: FOOL
lines.text: philosopher.
[_Exeunt Apemantus and Fool._]

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Pray you walk near. I’ll speak with you anon.
[_Exeunt Servants._]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You make me marvel wherefore ere this time

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Had you not fully laid my state before me,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: That I might so have rated my expense

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: As I had leave of means.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: You would not hear me,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: At many leisures I proposed.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Go to.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Perchance some single vantages you took

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: When my indisposition put you back,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And that unaptness made your minister

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Thus to excuse yourself.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: O my good lord,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: At many times I brought in my accounts,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Laid them before you; you would throw them off

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And say you found them in mine honesty.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: When for some trifling present you have bid me

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Return so much, I have shook my head and wept,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Yea, ’gainst th’ authority of manners, prayed you

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: To hold your hand more close. I did endure

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Not seldom nor no slight checks, when I have

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Prompted you in the ebb of your estate

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And your great flow of debts. My loved lord,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Though you hear now, too late, yet now’s a time.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: The greatest of your having lacks a half

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: To pay your present debts.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Let all my land be sold.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: ’Tis all engaged, some forfeited and gone,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And what remains will hardly stop the mouth

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Of present dues; the future comes apace.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: What shall defend the interim? And at length

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: How goes our reckoning?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To Lacedaemon did my land extend.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: O my good lord, the world is but a word;

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Were it all yours to give it in a breath,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: How quickly were it gone!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You tell me true.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: If you suspect my husbandry or falsehood,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Call me before th’ exactest auditors

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And set me on the proof. So the gods bless me,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: When all our offices have been oppressed

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: With riotous feeders, when our vaults have wept

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: With drunken spilth of wine, when every room

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Hath blazed with lights and brayed with minstrelsy,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I have retired me to a wasteful cock

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And set mine eyes at flow.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Prithee, no more.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Heavens, have I said, the bounty of this lord!

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: How many prodigal bits have slaves and peasants

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: This night englutted? Who is not Timon’s?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: What heart, head, sword, force, means, but is Lord Timon’s?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Great Timon, noble, worthy, royal Timon!

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Ah, when the means are gone that buy this praise,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: The breath is gone whereof this praise is made.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Feast-won, fast-lost; one cloud of winter showers,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: These flies are couched.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Come, sermon me no further.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: No villainous bounty yet hath passed my heart;

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Unwisely, not ignobly, have I given.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Why dost thou weep? Canst thou the conscience lack

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To think I shall lack friends? Secure thy heart.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: If I would broach the vessels of my love

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And try the argument of hearts by borrowing,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Men and men’s fortunes could I frankly use

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: As I can bid thee speak.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Assurance bless your thoughts!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And in some sort these wants of mine are crowned,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: That I account them blessings. For by these

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Shall I try friends. You shall perceive how you

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Mistake my fortunes. I am wealthy in my friends.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Within there! Flaminius! Servilius!
Enter Flaminius, Servilius and a third Servant.

lines.speaker: SERVANTS
lines.text: My lord, my lord.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I will dispatch you severally. [_To Servilius_.] You to Lord Lucius;
[_To Flaminius_.]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: to Lord Lucullus you, I hunted with his honour today;
[_To the third Servant_.]

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: you to Sempronius. Commend me to their loves;

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: and I am proud, say, that my occasions have found time to use ’em

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: toward a supply of money. Let the request be fifty talents.

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: As you have said, my lord.
[_Exeunt Servants._]
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Lord Lucius and Lucullus? Humh!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Go you, sir, to the senators,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Of whom, even to the state’s best health, I have

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Deserved this hearing, Bid ’em send o’ th’ instant

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: A thousand talents to me.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I have been bold—

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: For that I knew it the most general way—

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: To them to use your signet and your name,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: But they do shake their heads, and I am here

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: No richer in return.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Is’t true? Can’t be?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: They answer in a joint and corporate voice

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: That now they are at fall, want treasure, cannot

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Do what they would, are sorry. You are honourable,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: But yet they could have wished—they know not—

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Something hath been amiss—a noble nature

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: May catch a wrench—would all were well—’tis pity.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And so, intending other serious matters,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: After distasteful looks and these hard fractions,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: With certain half-caps and cold-moving nods

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: They froze me into silence.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You gods, reward them!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Prithee, man, look cheerly. These old fellows

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Have their ingratitude in them hereditary.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Their blood is caked, ’tis cold, it seldom flows;

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: ’Tis lack of kindly warmth they are not kind;

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And nature, as it grows again toward earth,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Is fashioned for the journey, dull and heavy.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Go to Ventidius. Prithee, be not sad,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Thou art true and honest, ingenuously I speak,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: No blame belongs to thee. Ventidius lately

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Buried his father, by whose death he’s stepped

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Into a great estate. When he was poor,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Imprisoned and in scarcity of friends,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I cleared him with five talents. Greet him from me,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Bid him suppose some good necessity

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Touches his friend, which craves to be remembered

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: With those five talents. That had, give’t these fellows

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To whom ’tis instant due. Ne’er speak, or think

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: That Timon’s fortunes ’mong his friends can sink.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I would I could not think it.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: That thought is bounty’s foe;

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Being free itself, it thinks all others so.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Athens. A room in Lucullus’ house

lines.text: Flaminius waiting to speak with Lucullus from his master.
Enter a Servant to him.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: I have told my lord of you; he is coming down to you.

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: I thank you, sir.
Enter Lucullus.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Here’s my lord.
[_Aside_.]

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: One of Lord Timon’s men? A gift, I warrant. Why, this hits

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: right. I dreamt of a silver basin and ewer tonight.—Flaminius, honest

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: Flaminius, you are very respectively welcome, sir. Fill me some wine.
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: And how does that honourable, complete, free-hearted gentleman of

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: Athens, thy very bountiful good lord and master?

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: His health is well, sir.

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: I am right glad that his health is well, sir. And what hast thou there

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: under thy cloak, pretty Flaminius?

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Faith, nothing but an empty box, sir, which in my lord’s behalf I come

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: to entreat your honour to supply; who, having great and instant

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: occasion to use fifty talents, hath sent to your lordship to furnish

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: him, nothing doubting your present assistance therein.

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: La, la, la, la! Nothing doubting, says he? Alas, good lord! A noble

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: gentleman ’tis, if he would not keep so good a house. Many a time and

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: often I ha’ dined with him, and told him on’t, and come again to supper

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: to him of purpose to have him spend less, and yet he would embrace no

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: counsel, take no warning by my coming. Every man has his fault, and

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: honesty is his. I ha’ told him on’t, but I could ne’er get him from ’t.
Enter Servant with wine.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Please your lordship, here is the wine.

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: Flaminius, I have noted thee always wise. Here’s to thee.

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Your lordship speaks your pleasure.

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: I have observed thee always for a towardly prompt spirit, give thee thy

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: due, and one that knows what belongs to reason, and canst use the time

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: well, if the time use thee well. Good parts in thee.
[_To Servant_.]

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: Get you gone, sirrah.—
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: Draw nearer, honest Flaminius. Thy lord’s a bountiful gentleman, but

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: thou art wise and thou know’st well enough, although thou com’st to me,

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: that this is no time to lend money, especially upon bare friendship

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: without security. Here’s three solidares for thee. Good boy, wink at

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: me, and say thou saw’st me not. Fare thee well.

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Is’t possible the world should so much differ,

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: And we alive that lived? Fly, damned baseness,

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: To him that worships thee.
[_Throws the money back._]

lines.speaker: LUCULLUS
lines.text: Ha! Now I see thou art a fool and fit for thy master.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: May these add to the number that may scald thee!

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Let molten coin be thy damnation,

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Thou disease of a friend, and not himself!

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Has friendship such a faint and milky heart

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: It turns in less than two nights? O you gods,

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: I feel my master’s passion. This slave

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Unto his honour has my lord’s meat in him.

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Why should it thrive and turn to nutriment

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: When he is turned to poison?

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: O, may diseases only work upon’t,

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: And when he’s sick to death, let not that part of nature

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Which my lord paid for be of any power

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: To expel sickness, but prolong his hour.
[_Exit._]
Enter Lucius with three Strangers.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Who, the Lord Timon? He is my very good friend and an honourable

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: gentleman.

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: We know him for no less, though we are but strangers to him. But I can

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: tell you one thing, my lord, and which I hear from common rumours: now

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Lord Timon’s happy hours are done and past, and his estate shrinks from

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: him.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Fie, no, do not believe it; he cannot want for money.

lines.speaker: SECOND STRANGER
lines.text: But believe you this, my lord, that, not long ago one of his men was

lines.speaker: SECOND STRANGER
lines.text: with the Lord Lucullus to borrow so many talents, nay, urged extremely

lines.speaker: SECOND STRANGER
lines.text: for’t, and showed what necessity belonged to’t, and yet was denied.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: How?

lines.speaker: SECOND STRANGER
lines.text: I tell you, denied, my lord.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: What a strange case was that! Now, before the gods, I am ashamed on’t.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Denied that honourable man? There was very little honour showed in’t.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For my own part, I must needs confess, I have received some small

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: kindnesses from him, as money, plate, jewels, and such like trifles,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: nothing comparing to his; yet had he mistook him, and sent to me, I

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: should ne’er have denied his occasion so many talents.
Enter Servilius.

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: See, by good hap, yonder’s my lord; I have sweat to see his honour.
[_To Lucius_.]

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: My honoured lord!

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Servilius? You are kindly met, sir. Fare thee well. Commend me to thy

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: honourable virtuous lord, my very exquisite friend.

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: May it please your honour, my lord hath sent—

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ha! What has he sent? I am so much endeared to that lord; he’s ever

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: sending. How shall I thank him, thinkest thou? And what has he sent

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: now?

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: Has only sent his present occasion now, my lord, requesting your

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: lordship to supply his instant use with so many talents.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I know his lordship is but merry with me;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: He cannot want fifty-five hundred talents.

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: But in the meantime he wants less, my lord.

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: If his occasion were not virtuous,

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: I should not urge it half so faithfully.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Dost thou speak seriously, Servilius?

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: Upon my soul, ’tis true, sir.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: What a wicked beast was I to disfurnish myself against such a good

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: time, when I might ha’ shown myself honourable! How unluckily it

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: happened that I should purchase the day before for a little part, and

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: undo a great deal of honour! Servilius, now before the gods, I am not

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: able to do—the more beast, I say—I was sending to use Lord Timon

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: myself, these gentlemen can witness; but I would not for the wealth of

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Athens I had done it now. Commend me bountifully to his good lordship,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: and I hope his honour will conceive the fairest of me, because I have

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: no power to be kind. And tell him this from me: I count it one of my

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: greatest afflictions, say, that I cannot pleasure such an honourable

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: gentleman. Good Servilius, will you befriend me so far as to use mine

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: own words to him?

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: Yes, sir, I shall.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I’ll look you out a good turn, Servilius.
[_Exit Servilius._]

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: True, as you said, Timon is shrunk indeed,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And he that’s once denied will hardly speed.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Do you observe this, Hostilius?

lines.speaker: SECOND STRANGER
lines.text: Ay, too well.

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Why, this is the world’s soul, and just of the same piece

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Is every flatterer’s spirit. Who can call him his friend

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: That dips in the same dish? For, in my knowing,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Timon has been this lord’s father

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: And kept his credit with his purse,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Supported his estate, nay, Timon’s money

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Has paid his men their wages. He ne’er drinks

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: But Timon’s silver treads upon his lip,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: And yet—O, see the monstrousness of man

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: When he looks out in an ungrateful shape—

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: He does deny him, in respect of his,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: What charitable men afford to beggars.

lines.speaker: THIRD STRANGER
lines.text: Religion groans at it.

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: For mine own part,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: I never tasted Timon in my life,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Nor came any of his bounties over me

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: To mark me for his friend. Yet I protest,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: For his right noble mind, illustrious virtue,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: And honourable carriage,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Had his necessity made use of me,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: I would have put my wealth into donation,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: And the best half should have returned to him,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: So much I love his heart. But I perceive

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: Men must learn now with pity to dispense,

lines.speaker: FIRST STRANGER
lines.text: For policy sits above conscience.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A room in Sempronius’ house

lines.text: Enter a Third Servant  of Timon’s with Sempronius, another of Timon’s friends.

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Must he needs trouble me in’t? Hum! ’Bove all others?

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: He might have tried Lord Lucius or Lucullus;

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: And now Ventidius is wealthy too,

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Whom he redeemed from prison. All these

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Owe their estates unto him.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: My lord,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: They have all been touched and found base metal,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: For they have all denied him.

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: How? Have they denied him?

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Has Ventidius and Lucullus denied him

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: And does he send to me? Three? Humh!

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: It shows but little love or judgment in him.

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Must I be his last refuge? His friends, like physicians,

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Thrive, give him over. Must I take th’ cure upon me?

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Has much disgraced me in’t. I’m angry at him,

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: That might have known my place. I see no sense for’t

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: But his occasions might have wooed me first;

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: For, in my conscience, I was the first man

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: That e’er received gift from him.

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: And does he think so backwardly of me now

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: That I’ll requite it last? No.

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: So it may prove an argument of laughter

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: To th’ rest, and I ’mongst lords be thought a fool.

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: I’d rather than the worth of thrice the sum

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Had sent to me first, but for my mind’s sake;

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: I’d such a courage to do him good. But now return,

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: And with their faint reply this answer join:

lines.speaker: SEMPRONIUS
lines.text: Who bates mine honour shall not know my coin.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Excellent! Your lordship’s a goodly villain. The devil knew not what he

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: did when he made man politic; he crossed himself by’t, and I cannot

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: think but, in the end the villainies of man will set him clear. How

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: fairly this lord strives to appear foul! Takes virtuous copies to be

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: wicked, like those that under hot ardent zeal would set whole realms on

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: fire.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Of such a nature is his politic love.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: This was my lord’s best hope, now all are fled

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Save only the gods. Now his friends are dead,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Doors that were ne’er acquainted with their wards

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Many a bounteous year must be employed

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Now to guard sure their master.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: And this is all a liberal course allows,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Who cannot keep his wealth must keep his house.
[_Exit._]
Enter two of Varro’s Servants meeting Titus and Hortensius and then Lucius, all Servants of Timon’s creditors, to wait for his coming out.
