lines.speaker: FIRST VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Well met, good morrow, Titus and Hortensius.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: The like to you, kind Varro.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: Lucius!

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: What, do we meet together?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ay, and I think

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: One business does command us all;

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: For mine is money.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: So is theirs and ours.
Enter Philotus.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And, sir, Philotus too!

lines.speaker: PHILOTUS
lines.text: Good day at once.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Welcome, good brother.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: What do you think the hour?

lines.speaker: PHILOTUS
lines.text: Labouring for nine.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: So much?

lines.speaker: PHILOTUS
lines.text: Is not my lord seen yet?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: PHILOTUS
lines.text: I wonder on’t, he was wont to shine at seven.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ay, but the days are waxed shorter with him.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: You must consider that a prodigal course

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Is like the sun’s, but not like his recoverable.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: I fear ’tis deepest winter in Lord Timon’s purse:

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: That is, one may reach deep enough, and yet

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Find little.

lines.speaker: PHILOTUS
lines.text: I am of your fear for that.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: I’ll show you how t’ observe a strange event.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Your lord sends now for money?

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: Most true, he does.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: And he wears jewels now of Timon’s gift,

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: For which I wait for money.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: It is against my heart.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Mark how strange it shows,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Timon in this should pay more than he owes,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And e’en as if your lord should wear rich jewels

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And send for money for ’em.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: I’m weary of this charge, the gods can witness.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: I know my lord hath spent of Timon’s wealth,

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: And now ingratitude makes it worse than stealth.

lines.speaker: FIRST VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Yes, mine’s three thousand crowns. What’s yours?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Five thousand mine.

lines.speaker: FIRST VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: ’Tis much deep, and it should seem by th’ sum

lines.speaker: FIRST VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Your master’s confidence was above mine,

lines.speaker: FIRST VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: Else surely his had equalled.
Enter Flaminius.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: One of Lord Timon’s men.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Flaminius? Sir, a word. Pray, is my lord ready to come forth?

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: No, indeed he is not.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: We attend his lordship; pray, signify so much.

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: I need not tell him that, he knows you are too diligent.
[_Exit Flaminius._]
Enter Flavius in a cloak, muffled.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ha, is not that his steward muffled so?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: He goes away in a cloud. Call him, call him.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Do you hear, sir?

lines.speaker: SECOND VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: By your leave, sir.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: What do you ask of me, my friend?

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: We wait for certain money here, sir.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Ay,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: If money were as certain as your waiting,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: ’Twere sure enough.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Why then preferred you not your sums and bills

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: When your false masters eat of my lord’s meat?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Then they could smile and fawn upon his debts,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: And take down th’ interest into their gluttonous maws.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: You do yourselves but wrong to stir me up,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Let me pass quietly.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Believe’t, my lord and I have made an end,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I have no more to reckon, he to spend.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Ay, but this answer will not serve.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: If ’twill not serve, ’tis not so base as you,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: For you serve knaves.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: FIRST VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: How? What does his cashiered worship mutter?

lines.speaker: SECOND VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: No matter what, he’s poor, and that’s revenge enough. Who can speak

lines.speaker: SECOND VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: broader than he that has no house to put his head in? Such may rail

lines.speaker: SECOND VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: against great buildings.
Enter Servilius.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: O, here’s Servilius; now we shall know some answer.

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: If I might beseech you, gentlemen, to repair some other hour, I should

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: derive much from’t. For take’t of my soul, my lord leans wondrously to

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: discontent. His comfortable temper has forsook him, he’s much out of

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: health and keeps his chamber.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Many do keep their chambers are not sick.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And if it be so far beyond his health,

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Methinks he should the sooner pay his debts

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: And make a clear way to the gods.

lines.speaker: SERVILIUS
lines.text: Good gods!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: We cannot take this for answer, sir.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: FLAMINIUS
lines.text: Servilius, help! My lord, my lord!
Enter Timon in a rage.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What, are my doors opposed against my passage?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Have I been ever free, and must my house

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Be my retentive enemy, my jail?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: The place which I have feasted, does it now,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Like all mankind, show me an iron heart?

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Put in now, Titus.

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: My lord, here is my bill.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Here’s mine.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: And mine, my lord.

lines.speaker: BOTH VARRO’S SERVANTS
lines.text: And ours, my lord.

lines.speaker: PHILOTUS
lines.text: All our bills.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Knock me down with ’em! Cleave me to the girdle.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Alas, my lord—

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Cut my heart in sums!

lines.speaker: TITUS
lines.text: Mine, fifty talents.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Tell out my blood.

lines.speaker: LUCIUS
lines.text: Five thousand crowns, my lord.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Five thousand drops pays that. What yours, and yours?

lines.speaker: FIRST VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: My lord—

lines.speaker: SECOND VARRO’S SERVANT
lines.text: My lord—

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Tear me, take me, and the gods fall upon you!
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: Faith, I perceive our masters may throw their caps at their money.

lines.speaker: HORTENSIUS
lines.text: These debts may well be called desperate ones, for a madman owes ’em.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Timon and Flavius.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: They have e’en put my breath from me, the slaves.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Creditors? Devils!

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: My dear lord—

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What if it should be so?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: My lord—

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I’ll have it so.—My steward!

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Here, my lord.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: So fitly? Go, bid all my friends again,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Lucius, Lucullus, and Sempronius, all.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I’ll once more feast the rascals.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: O my lord,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: You only speak from your distracted soul;

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: There is not so much left to furnish out

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: A moderate table.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Be it not in thy care. Go,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I charge thee, invite them all. Let in the tide

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Of knaves once more. My cook and I’ll provide.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter three Senators at one door, Alcibiades meeting them, with Attendants.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: My lord, you have my voice to ’t. The fault’s

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Bloody. ’Tis necessary he should die.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Nothing emboldens sin so much as mercy.

lines.speaker: SECOND SENATOR
lines.text: Most true, the law shall bruise ’em.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Honour, health, and compassion to the senate!

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Now, captain?

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: I am a humble suitor to your virtues,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: For pity is the virtue of the law,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: And none but tyrants use it cruelly.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: It pleases time and fortune to lie heavy

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Upon a friend of mine, who in hot blood

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Hath stepped into the law, which is past depth

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: To those that without heed do plunge into’t.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: He is a man, setting his fate aside,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Of comely virtues,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Nor did he soil the fact with cowardice—

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: An honour in him which buys out his fault—

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: But with a noble fury and fair spirit,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Seeing his reputation touched to death,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: He did oppose his foe;

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: And with such sober and unnoted passion

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: He did behave his anger, ere ’twas spent,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: As if he had but proved an argument.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: You undergo too strict a paradox,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Striving to make an ugly deed look fair.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Your words have took such pains as if they laboured

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: To bring manslaughter into form and set quarrelling

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Upon the head of valour, which indeed

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: Is valour misbegot and came into the world

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: When sects and factions were newly born.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: He’s truly valiant that can wisely suffer

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: The worst that man can breathe, and make his wrongs

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: His outsides to wear them like his raiment, carelessly,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: And ne’er prefer his injuries to his heart,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: To bring it into danger.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: If wrongs be evils and enforce us kill,

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: What folly ’tis to hazard life for ill!

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: My lord—

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: You cannot make gross sins look clear.

lines.speaker: FIRST SENATOR
lines.text: To revenge is no valour, but to bear.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: My lords, then, under favour, pardon me

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: If I speak like a captain.

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Why do fond men expose themselves to battle

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: And not endure all threats? Sleep upon’t,

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: And let the foes quietly cut their throats

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Without repugnancy? If there be

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Such valour in the bearing, what make we

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: Abroad? Why, then, women are more valiant

lines.speaker: ALCIBIADES
lines.text: That stay at home, if bearing carry it,

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Where wouldst thou send it?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: To sauce thy dishes.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: The middle of humanity thou never knewest, but the extremity of both

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: ends. When thou wast in thy gilt and thy perfume, they mocked thee for

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: too much curiosity; in thy rags thou know’st none, but art despised for

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: the contrary. There’s a medlar for thee. Eat it.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: On what I hate I feed not.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Dost hate a medlar?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Ay, though it look like thee.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: An thou’dst hated medlars sooner, thou shouldst have loved thyself

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: better now. What man didst thou ever know unthrift that was beloved

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: after his means?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Who, without those means thou talk’st of, didst thou ever know beloved?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Myself.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: I understand thee. Thou hadst some means to keep a dog.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: What things in the world canst thou nearest compare to thy flatterers?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Women nearest; but men—men are the things themselves. What wouldst thou

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: do with the world, Apemantus, if it lay in thy power?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Give it the beasts, to be rid of the men.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Wouldst thou have thyself fall in the confusion of men and remain a

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: beast with the beasts?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Ay, Timon.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: A beastly ambition, which the gods grant thee t’ attain to. If thou

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: wert the lion, the fox would beguile thee; if thou wert the lamb, the

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: fox would eat thee; if thou wert the fox, the lion would suspect thee

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: when peradventure thou wert accused by the ass; if thou wert the ass,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: thy dulness would torment thee, and still thou lived’st but as a

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: breakfast to the wolf; if thou wert the wolf, thy greediness would

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: afflict thee, and oft thou shouldst hazard thy life for thy dinner.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Wert thou the unicorn, pride and wrath would confound thee and make

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: thine own self the conquest of thy fury; wert thou a bear, thou wouldst

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: be killed by the horse; wert thou a horse, thou wouldst be seized by

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: the leopard; wert thou a leopard, thou wert germane to the lion, and

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: the spots of thy kindred were jurors on thy life. All thy safety were

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: remotion, and thy defence absence. What beast couldst thou be that were

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: not subject to a beast? And what beast art thou already that seest not

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: thy loss in transformation!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: If thou couldst please me with speaking to me, thou mightst have hit

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: upon it here. The commonwealth of Athens is become a forest of beasts.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How has the ass broke the wall, that thou art out of the city?

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Yonder comes a poet and a painter. The plague of company light upon

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: thee! I will fear to catch it, and give way. When I know not what else

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: to do, I’ll see thee again.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: When there is nothing living but thee, thou shalt be welcome. I had

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: rather be a beggar’s dog than Apemantus.

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: Thou art the cap of all the fools alive.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Would thou wert clean enough to spit upon!

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS
lines.text: A plague on thee! Thou art too bad to curse.

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: If I name thee,

lines.text: I would my tongue could rot them off!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Away, thou issue of a mangy dog!

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Lie where the light foam of the sea may beat

lines.speaker: TIMON

[_To the gold._]

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: APEMANTUS

lines.speaker: FIRST BANDIT

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: His antidotes are poison, and he slays

lines.text: More than you rob. Take wealth and lives together,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Do villainy, do, since you protest to do’t,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Like workmen. I’ll example you with thievery.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: The sun’s a thief and with his great attraction

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Robs the vast sea; the moon’s an arrant thief,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: And her pale fire she snatches from the sun;

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: That feeds and breeds by a composture stol’n

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: From general excrement. Each thing’s a thief.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: The laws, your curb and whip, in their rough power

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Has unchecked theft. Love not yourselves; away!

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Rob one another. There’s more gold. Cut throats,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: All that you meet are thieves. To Athens go,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Break open shops, nothing can you steal

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: But thieves do lose it. Steal no less for this I give you,

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.text: Has almost charmed me from my profession by persuading me to it.

lines.speaker: FIRST BANDIT
lines.text: ’Tis in the malice of mankind that he thus advises us, not to have us

lines.speaker: FIRST BANDIT
lines.text: thrive in our mystery.

lines.speaker: SECOND BANDIT
lines.text: I’ll believe him as an enemy and give over my trade.

lines.speaker: FIRST BANDIT
lines.text: Let us first see peace in Athens. There is no time so miserable but a

Enter Flavius.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: What, dost thou weep? Come nearer then. I love thee

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Because thou art a woman and disclaim’st

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Flinty mankind, whose eyes do never give

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: I beg of you to know me, good my lord,

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: T’ accept my grief, and whilst this poor wealth lasts

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Had I a steward

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: So true, so just, and now so comfortable?

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: It almost turns my dangerous nature mild.

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Let me behold thy face. Surely this man

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Forgive my general and exceptless rashness,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: You perpetual sober gods! I do proclaim

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: How fain would I have hated all mankind,

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: A usuring kindness and as rich men deal gifts,

lines.speaker: TIMON
lines.text: Expecting in return twenty for one?

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: No, my most worthy master, in whose breast

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS
lines.text: Doubt and suspect, alas, are placed too late.

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS

lines.speaker: FLAVIUS

lines.text: Look thee, ’tis so! Thou singly honest man,
